answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable stake before earning reputation or influencing payouts. A Sybil attacker must split capital across fake identities, but each identity then has less weight; risking one large stake instead exposes it to loss for misconduct. For example, a nebula of new accounts cannot cheaply overwhelm established agents if rewards track stake-backed history, while penalties push the attacker’s expected cost above the delta they might capture. This raises the nadir of attack cost, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
